Rangers receive excellent Dujon Sterling update as McInnes explains Kilmarnock withdrawal

By
Sam Groves
-
October 15, 2026
0

    Sponsored by

    Instaread

    Ibrox Noise, like most other Rangers fans, was delighted to hear the great Dujon Sterling Rangers fitness news.

    ADVERTISEMENT

    Naturally, as we all know, Rangers’ top choice right back was withdrawn at half time for minutes management against Kilmarnock.

    0:00 / 0:00

    >

    This changed the game entirely and saw a much deteriorated second half performance.

    However, Derek McInnes has given the full reason why Sterling was removed. It wasn’t, in actual fact, just to do with minutes management.

    ADVERTISEMENT

    He was, in fact, ill, with tonsillitis.

    Sterling’s illness

    Dujon Sterling had had an infection in the days leading up to the weekend’s fixture.

    The timing could have been better, but he managed the first 45. Of course, during that first 45, we saw a fairly solid and robust Rangers.

    ADVERTISEMENT

    Unfortunately, the introduction of Nedeljkovic disrupted the flow entirely, and Rangers were far less assured in the second 45.

    But the good news is that Sterling is fit.

    He did have that knock in training, a small hamstring pull, which he was able to get over, but then had the unfortunate double whammy of picking up tonsillitis a few days later.

    ADVERTISEMENT

    He was feeling, to quote McInnes, “under the weather”.

    Sensible management from McInnes

    He managed the first 45, but McInnes deemed that he should take the rest of the match out purely for recovery and minutes management.

    This was sensible management.

    As much as we want to see Sterling in the shirt doing his very, very solid thing in the rearguard, his health comes first.

    Not only did he have a niggle of an injury, which we believe now is not a problem, but he’d had the double whammy of being ill.

    He has now fully recovered from that and is set to feature for Rangers this weekend at Den Park v Dundee.

    Sterling’s importance to Rangers

    This is excellent news for Rangers because, quite frankly, Nedeljkovic is nowhere near up for it.

    Sterling is one of Rangers’ most in form players at the moment, and he’s a crucial part of why the team is doing as well as it is.

    Who could ever have known that Sterling would have bloomed into such an assured right back?

    Yes, he will never give the overlapping assists and goals that James Tavernier did, but your right back isn’t supposed to do that.

    They can chip in every now and again, but their job is to defend, defend on the right, and to say the least, Sterling does this with aplomb.

    Excellent news for the Rangers defence

    So we are delighted to hear that he is in good fettle and is ready for the next fixture.

    Consequently, we can feel assured that the Rangers rearguard will remain as robust as it has been of late.
